correctness.rationale: Exact gamma-integral expression and triangular specialization fix normalization. Fixed-index exponent derivative is 2C_n/T_n², second frequency derivative is 2/T_n². Two analytic branches split by ±sqrt(2C_n epsilon)+O(epsilon). Locally uniform differentiable incomplete-gamma expansion yields 1-e^lambda cos(s), whose only two roots in [-pi,pi] are simple for finite lambda>0; C¹ convergence proves exactly two nearby real zeros and excludes others. The packaged checker agrees, but finite tests do not prove infinite limits.

value.rationale: The quantity is a natural spectral-notch separation invariant for an infinitely degenerate triangular Fourier window. The precise exponential-frequency crossover demonstrates noncommuting small-perturbation/high-frequency limits not captured by qualitative Pólya placement or ordinary perturbation theory. The limit arccos(e^-lambda) provides a meaningful uniform profile across a whole parameter family, rather than an arbitrary finite slice.
